question.text: A hedger should choose futures over options when:

answer.text: They want to lock in a rate with certainty and don't need upside potential
They want to keep the possibility of benefiting from favorable rate movements
They have a very uncertain exposure amount
They expect high volatility in the near term

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures provide rate certainty and do not require an option premium, but they involve margin and mark-to-market obligations and give up favorable movement. Options cost a premium but preserve upside and flexibility (the put-option hedger retains the chance to benefit if USDINR moves favorably). The Trap: Futures are not "no cost" — p.61 highlights margin and mark-to-market operational obligations. The accurate contrast is "no option premium," not "no cost." Note: Futures = rate certainty, no option premium, foregone upside. Options = upside preserved, premium paid. The choice depends on the hedger's risk tolerance and cost sensitivity. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.61, 98, and 116-117.
